search_boundary.rule: Only sources independent of Layer-ROM candidate performance are eligible. Measurement/product requirements, numerical closure criteria, case-specific achieved errors, and generic goodness-of-fit thresholds are not automatically application tolerances.

sources.citation: Barnett B, Townley LR, Post V, Evans RE, Hunt RJ, Peeters L, Richardson S, Werner AD, Knapton A, Boronkay A (2012). Australian groundwater modelling guidelines. Waterlines Report Series No. 82. National Water Commission, Canberra.
extracted_authority: Model objectives and intended use should be defined early and should drive design, calibration, prediction and uncertainty analysis.
Performance measures should be agreed prior to calibration.
Generic SRMS targets such as 5% or 10% are meaningful only when achievability is known for the specific problem, environment and data density.
Model water-balance error below 1% is a numerical/accounting quality criterion, not an allowed recharge-representation error.

sources.citation: Jyrkama MI, Sykes JF (2006). Sensitivity and uncertainty analysis of the recharge boundary condition. Water Resources Research 42. doi:10.1029/2005WR004408.
extracted_authority: Recharge uncertainty can be propagated to prediction-specific groundwater head or pumping-well flow consequences using a groundwater-model sensitivity/reliability formulation.
The sensitivity is spatially dependent and tied to a specified prediction target.

sources.citation: Knowling MJ, Werner AD (2016). Estimability of recharge through groundwater model calibration: Insights from a field-scale steady-state example. Journal of Hydrology 540, 973-987. doi:10.1016/j.jhydrol.2016.07.003.
extracted_authority: In the specific synthetic regional example, average recharge error below 10% required extensive hydraulic-property information.
The study presents a benchmark for recharge estimability, not a normative application acceptance threshold.

sources.citation: Fan et al. (2023). Groundwater Sensitivity to Climate Variations Across Australia. Water Resources Research. doi:10.1029/2023WR035036.
extracted_authority: Groundwater-head sensitivity to precipitation and recharge-related forcing varies substantially across sites.
A single recharge-to-head error conversion is therefore not portable across groundwater systems.

sources.citation: Crosbie RS et al. (2005). A time series approach to inferring groundwater recharge using the water table fluctuation method. Water Resources Research. doi:10.1029/2004WR003077.
extracted_authority: Recharge estimates in the demonstrated method are materially sensitive to time step and specific yield assumptions.
The result supports explicit temporal semantics but does not define an acceptable Layer-ROM recharge error.

sources.citation: Effects of temporal resolution on modelled regional groundwater salinity and salt fluxes to surface water (2026). Computers & Geosciences / linked ScienceDirect record.
extracted_authority: In the studied low-lying coastal groundwater system, yearly recharge aggregation failed to preserve important seasonal groundwater-surface-water flux behavior; monthly forcing retained the relevant seasonal patterns better.
This is application- and system-specific evidence for the importance of temporal allocation, not a universal monthly acceptance rule.

sources.citation: Evaluating, interpreting, and communicating performance of hydrologic/water quality models considering intended use: A review and recommendations (2014). Environmental Modelling & Software. doi:10.1016/j.envsoft.2014.02.013.
extracted_authority: Model-performance interpretation should depend on intended use rather than a context-free universal score.

sources.citation: Hydrological Processes discussion of model plausibility, invalidation and fitness-for-purpose (2022), doi represented by source record 10.1002/hyp.14704.
extracted_authority: Fitness criteria should be agreed for the project purpose before evaluation.
Observation uncertainty should be assessed independently rather than silently equated with model-fidelity requirements.

sources.citation: Validation of Soil Moisture Data Products from the NASA SMAP Mission (NASA NTRS, 2021 record).
extracted_authority: SMAP defines an unbiased RMSE requirement below 0.04 m3/m3 for its soil-moisture product validation.

sources.citation: Walker et al. (2026). Modeling soil moisture from rainfall: An evaluation of the diagnostic soil moisture equation. Vadose Zone Journal. doi:10.1002/vzj2.70085.
extracted_authority: Independent station validation reports depth-specific soil-moisture RMSE magnitudes and stronger errors at wet/dry extremes.
Reported performance is empirical and model-specific; it does not prescribe acceptable process-profile error for scientific Layer-ROM use.

provenance_decision: No source in the reviewed set provides a directly transferable absolute Layer-ROM acceptance tolerance with purpose-matched temporal semantics for GW-R, GW-D or SCI-P.
prohibited_reuse: Do not use groundwater-model numerical water-balance closure as recharge-representation tolerance.
Do not use SMAP 0.04 m3/m3 as a process-model profile tolerance.
Do not use the Knowling and Werner <10% case result as a universal recharge acceptance threshold.
Do not derive a portable recharge-to-head tolerance from site-specific sensitivities.
Do not choose a threshold by inspecting L4/L6/R8 outcomes.
